source.archive: Cui, Li, and Zhou OSF replication archive
source.source_article: O’Connor, Effron, and Lucas (2020), Moral cleansing as hypocrisy: When private acts of charity make you feel better than you deserve
authorized_normalizations: Removed the archive's generic LLM wrapper, browser-behavior instruction, and all reason-generation requests.
Separated the common TaylorGroup and Joseph Larson frame from the tobacco/gambling business and volunteering combinations.
Locked items 15-19 as the primary hypocrisy composite and deterministic reverse-scoring of the genuine item.
Retained all 19 source items; praise, employment/harm, and character judgments remain secondary.

population.simulation_target: U.S. undergraduate evaluating an executive's private volunteering and business conduct

materials.participant_role: Act as one U.S. undergraduate participant evaluating Joseph Larson. Respond for yourself, do not predict the average person, and do not analyze the experiment.
materials.common_scenario: The TaylorGroup is a Houston consulting organization. Joseph Larson is its executive vice-president of accounting. The company's business and Larson's anonymous pro-bono volunteering and donations are described below.

inconsistent_tobacco.label: Inconsistent virtue: tobacco
inconsistent_tobacco.stimulus: The TaylorGroup helps tobacco companies increase tobacco sales and consumer growth, including in targeted communities. Larson privately works 10 pro-bono hours each weekend on anti-tobacco campaigns and anonymously donates $1,000 annually to organizations treating tobacco addiction and health effects.

inconsistent_gambling.label: Inconsistent virtue: gambling
inconsistent_gambling.stimulus: The TaylorGroup helps casinos increase gambling revenue and patron growth, including in lower-income target markets. Larson privately works 10 pro-bono hours each weekend on anti-gambling campaigns and anonymously donates $1,000 annually to organizations treating gambling addiction and adverse outcomes.

unrelated_tobacco_business_gambling_virt.label: Unrelated virtue: tobacco business and gambling volunteering
unrelated_tobacco_business_gambling_virt.stimulus: The TaylorGroup helps tobacco companies increase tobacco sales and consumer growth, including in targeted communities. Larson privately works 10 pro-bono hours each weekend on anti-gambling campaigns and anonymously donates $1,000 annually to organizations treating gambling addiction and adverse outcomes.

unrelated_gambling_business_tobacco_virt.label: Unrelated virtue: gambling business and tobacco volunteering
unrelated_gambling_business_tobacco_virt.stimulus: The TaylorGroup helps casinos increase gambling revenue and patron growth, including in lower-income target markets. Larson privately works 10 pro-bono hours each weekend on anti-tobacco campaigns and anonymously donates $1,000 annually to organizations treating tobacco addiction and health effects.

materials.response_instruction: Rate all 19 items from 1 to 7 using their stated anchors and return only integer item responses in the required JSON structure.

items.text: If Larson were looking for another job, organizations definitely should not hire him.
How do you view Larson? Use 1 for cruel and 7 for kind.
How do you view Larson? Use 1 for nice and 7 for awful.
How do you view Larson? Use 1 for cold and 7 for warm.
How do you view Larson? Use 1 for honest and 7 for dishonest.
How do you view Larson? Use 1 for unfair and 7 for fair.
How do you view Larson? Use 1 for moral and 7 for immoral.
How do you view Larson? Use 1 for arrogant and 7 for humble.
How do you view Larson? Use 1 for good and 7 for bad.
How do you view Larson? Use 1 for likable and 7 for dislikable.

research_restricted.aligned_hypothesis_text: Inconsistent moral cleansing produces higher hypocrisy judgments than unrelated private virtue, averaging across tobacco and gambling domains.
research_restricted.reversed_hypothesis_text: Unrelated private virtue produces higher hypocrisy judgments than inconsistent moral cleansing, averaging across tobacco and gambling domains.
